title: Readability: clearer names in is_followed
bug: `GET /me/following/<id>` answers whether they follow you, not you them.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR renamed variables but also inverted the logic in `is_followed` from `user.is_following(followed_user)` to `other.is_following(me)`, changing who is checked as the follower and causing 404 to become 204 for alice_follow, bob_follow_alice, carol_unfollow.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR renamed variables but also inverted the logic in `is_followed` from `user.is_following(followed_user)` to `other.is_following(me)`, changing who is checked as the follower and causing 404 to become 204 for alice_follow, bob_follow_alice, carol_unfollow.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR renamed variables but also inverted the logic in `is_followed` from `user.is_following(followed_user)` to `other.is_following(me)`, changing who is checked as the follower and causing 404 to become 204 for alice_follow, bob_follow_alice, carol_unfollow.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The same logic inversion causes dave_follow_all to receive 404 instead of 204 because the check now asks if the target user follows the current user instead of the reverse.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The same logic inversion causes dave_follow_all to receive 404 instead of 204 because the check now asks if the target user follows the current user instead of the reverse.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The same logic inversion causes dave_follow_all to receive 404 instead of 204 because the check now asks if the target user follows the current user instead of the reverse.

doppel.summary: The PR inadvertently reversed the follow-check logic while renaming variables, turning intended 404s into 204s and vice versa for multiple personas.

personas.name: alice_follow
personas.goal: Follow carol and verify the is_followed endpoint returns 204

personas.name: bob_follow_alice
personas.goal: Follow alice and check is_followed with reversed direction

personas.name: carol_no_follow
personas.goal: Do not follow anyone; just verify feed and following lists are empty

personas.name: dave_follow_all
personas.goal: Follow everyone and then verify is_followed for each

personas.goal: Create a post and verify it appears in the feed

personas.name: frank_bad_post
personas.goal: Send a post with empty text to trigger validation error

personas.name: alice_power_user
personas.goal: Follow many users, post multiple times, and verify feed ordering

personas.name: bob_careless_put
personas.goal: Send PUT /posts with missing text to trigger validation error

personas.name: carol_unfollow
personas.goal: Follow then unfollow a user and verify removal

personas.name: dave_feed_after_unfollow
personas.goal: Unfollow one user and verify feed excludes that user's posts

review.why: The PR inverts the follow-check logic: it now returns 404 when the target user does NOT follow the current user, whereas the original correctly returned 404 when the current user does NOT follow the target. This changes the API's behavior for the /api/users/me/followed/<id> endpoint.

suspicions.claim: The is_followed endpoint now checks if the target user follows the current user instead of the current user following the target user
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create two users A and B where A follows B but B does not follow A. 2. Authenticate as user A. 3. Call GET /api/me/following/<B's id>. 4. Before PR: returns 204 (A follows B). After PR: returns 404 (B does not follow A).
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me/following/2 returned 204 in both base and head, showing the endpoint still checks if the current user follows the target user.
